verdict: Within a single signal's ranking, magnitude adds NO incremental gold/negative discrimination beyond ordinal position (ΔAUC ≤ 0 with CIs spanning zero on all three datasets). This null is informative rather than contradictory: per-signal scores are monotone in their own ranks, so their relevance content is already expressed ordinally. The utility of magnitude that our fusion experiments observe therefore arises at the CROSS-SIGNAL level — when two signals' magnitudes are combined on heterogeneous scales, the relative magnitudes across signals (which no single-signal ranking encodes) change which document wins after fusion. Relevance-bearing magnitude is thus a property of the pair geometry, not of either component alone — precisely the joint-geometry thesis.
